name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.228.0 — The depended_on_by frontmatter field is retired: both spec templates stop emitting it and doctor's renumber remedy rewrites only the depends_on entries that name the spec. depends_on is the single home for dependency links; nothing in the pipeline ever read the back-link, and existing specs may keep their old lines. 7.227.0 — Test expiry's --apply now lands through the host's gateCommand: after writing, it runs the gate in the host root, and a red gate restores every trimmed and deleted file byte-for-byte, names the gate with its output tail, and exits 1 (--keep-on-red keeps the writes to fix forward; a host with no gateCommand gets a warning). The shared file walk skips git-ignored paths, so a built dist/ no longer changes what the sweep keeps, and the invariant keep-clause matches a script's basename as a whole name (catalog.json no longer names log.js). A dry run and an apply over the same committed tree now report the same counts in any checkout. 7.226.0 — A keep-forever criterion that points at an existing test with → reuses now counts as covered in the review matrix and the drift check, and protects that test from the expiry sweep, whatever id the test carries; one shared reader resolves the pointer. The test scanner reads table cases (it.each, test.for) and modifier chains (only, skip, concurrent, sequential, fails, todo, fixme) as cases, so the sweep counts and reports them and never deletes a file that still holds one. A File Plan row naming a bare root-level file (Dockerfile) is a path when its row carries a file action. Doctor's ledger check reads known stages from the fleet reader instead of a second list.
